judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short sentences; 'unless otherwise indicated' is a soft qualifier but the rule is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies the Coinsurance Additional Condition to the Extensions, which must be squared with the Coinsurance condition itself (c065) and with Limits Of Insurance, though the carve-out is expressly drafted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare cross-reference to the Causes of Loss form; nothing to interpret.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations identify CP 10 30 Special Form, so the pointer resolves without difficulty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The most we will pay for loss or damage in any one occurrence is the applicable Limit of Insurance' is terse, and 'applicable' does real work where a single blanket limit covers nine buildings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be reconciled with the blanket limits in the Declarations, with the Additional Coverages that are 'additional insurance', and with the Coinsurance condition, which can reduce recovery below the stated limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An ordered calculation with two worked examples; the sequence (coinsurance first, then deductible) is spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly keyed to the Coinsurance Condition and the Agreed Value Optional Coverage, and consistent with the Coinsurance steps in c065.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence applicability statement; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the parallel statements introducing the Commercial Property Conditions and the Additional Conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Eight words, entirely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with Loss Payment a.(3), under which the insurer may elect to take property at an agreed or appraised value.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As printed the text is badly scrambled (the 'Pay its chosen appraiser' limb is lost), and 'competent and impartial appraiser' is a standard but contestable qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 F expressly replaces the Appraisal Loss Condition with a version making appraisal available only if both parties voluntarily agree, so this mandatory-on-demand version directly contradicts the controlling Kansas endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Contains soft temporal standards — 'prompt notice', 'as soon as possible', 'as often as may be reasonably required' — whose boundaries are the classic post-loss battleground.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with Loss Payment, which conditions payment on compliance, and with Legal Action Against Us, which requires 'full compliance with all of the terms'; the duties are parallel to the Business Income duties condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At our option' gives the insurer four alternatives, and paragraph b. excludes ordinance-or-law increased cost — a limitation whose reach against the Increased Cost of Construction coverage is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the Valuation condition, the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage and Additional Coverage e.(9), which says the Loss Payment and Valuation conditions do not include code-upgrade cost while the ICC amount is not subject to that limitation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, mechanical recovery-of-property rule; 'at your option' is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Transfer Of Rights Of Recovery and with Limits Of Insurance, to which it is expressly subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Vacant', 'customary operations' and the 31%-of-square-footage test are defined with unusual care, though 'customary operations' still carries some looseness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interlocks with the Vacancy Provisions (c062) and with the Business Income definition of 'operations', which includes tenantability of the premises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise 60-day trigger, a closed list of barred perils and a fixed 15% reduction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends entirely on the definitions in c061 and interacts with the rental-value coverage where units in an apartment complex may be untenanted; the pieces are drafted to fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Actual cash value' is the central valuation term and is left undefined in this form, and the $2,500 repair threshold and the improvements-and-betterments proration add further contestable mechanics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 B supplies a definition of 'Actual Cash Value' and the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage substitutes replacement cost for ACV, so three provisions must be harmonised to know what this condition actually requires.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence applicability statement; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the Loss Conditions lead-in; no tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The four-step formula turns on 'the value of Covered Property at the time of loss' — an undefined valuation basis (ACV or replacement cost?) — and on 'the Limit of Insurance for the property' where a single blanket limit covers nine buildings; the printed text also drops the end of Step (2).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be squared with the blanket 100% coinsurance entries in the Declarations, the Deductible ordering rule, the Agreed Value and Inflation Guard Optional Coverages, and the blanket-limit variant of the Increased Cost of Construction cap in c042, which itself uses 'the applicable coinsurance percentage'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As reproduced the Mortgageholders condition is spliced mid-sentence with the Agreed Value and Inflation Guard Optional Coverages, so several sentences are incomplete and the numbering does not track.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The interleaved Agreed Value and Inflation Guard text bears on the Coinsurance condition and the Limit of Insurance, and the Declarations show a 4% Inflation Guard, so the merged material has real cross-provision consequences.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence stripping code-upgrade cost out of replacement cost; the words are plain but the sentence is unqualified and sits alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts, or at least must be reconciled with, Additional Coverage A.4.e (Increased Cost Of Construction), which applies only where Replacement Cost applies and whose e.(9) says the Replacement Cost provision's exclusion of code-upgrade cost does not limit the ICC amount.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional on the Declarations showing the Extension; the valuation-by-contract limitation is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly deletes Paragraph 3.b.(1) of the Replacement Cost Optional Coverage, which is a coordinated amendment rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A circular definition ('fungus means any type or form of fungus') that nonetheless enumerates its inclusions clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches the identical definitions in CP 10 30 G.1 and CG 21 67 C, so the term is used consistently across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant' followed by a specific list is the paradigm general-versus-specific definition, routinely fought over on ejusdem grounds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same definition appears in CP 00 30 F.4 and CGL Definition 15, so the instrument at least uses it consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition with enumerated categories; no realistic ambiguity for an apartment risk.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Property Not Covered, Valuation c. and the Replacement Cost exclusions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Identical in substance to c005; a simple grant of a cancellation right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is a second printing of the same condition in the cover jacket; the duplication itself is untidy but the texts match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear 10/30-day notice periods; nothing indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 02 61 A replaces Paragraph 2 of the Cancellation Common Policy Condition for Kansas, adding a reasons requirement and restricting grounds after 90 days, so this printed text is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence mailing rule; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical to c007 and consistent with IL 02 61 B.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two flat sentences fixing the cancellation date; the OCR 'and' for 'end' is an artifact, not a drafting error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c008 without variation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same short-rate indeterminacy as c009 ('may be less than pro rata'), otherwise mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c009 verbatim; no other provision fixes the refund basis.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single evidentiary sentence; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c010 and matches IL 02 61 B.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Integration plus no-oral-modification; the tension between 'contains all the agreements' and the insured's authority to make changes is mild and conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c011; the policy is in fact amended only by issued endorsements, which is what the clause requires.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite as to scope and period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c012 and squares with the CGL Premium Audit record-keeping duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Reads 'We have the right but are not obligated to', which is internally coherent, and the disclaimers are enumerated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The other printing at c013 states the right without the 'not obligated' qualifier in the same sentence and adds a boiler/pressure-vessel/elevator carve-out that this version omits, so the two versions of one condition differ.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short numbered duties; entirely definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c014 and coheres with the CGL Premium Audit condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An anti-assignment rule with a death exception; the printing says 'our legal representative' where 'your' is meant, a small slip that could matter.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c015 (which reads 'your legal representative'), so the two printings of the same condition differ on whose representative is meant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'We will assume you no longer want the insurance' is a deeming rule; otherwise mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This printing says the notice will specify 'the date of cancellation' whereas c016 says 'the date and time', and neither mentions the reasons requirement imposed by IL 02 61.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence applicability statement; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is fuller than the truncated version at c017, listing the Common Policy Conditions and the coverage-form Loss and Additional Conditions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Void in any case of fraud' is severe but standard; materiality is a fact question rather than a construction problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: IL 01 60 (Kansas Changes) expressly replaces this condition with a narrower non-payment remedy, so this printed text is contradicted by the controlling endorsement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two definite sentences; 'beyond your direction or control' is workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 C.2 supersedes this condition where townhouse coverage is provided, leaving a narrow question whether the substitution reaches these apartment buildings.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single anti-stacking sentence with no open term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c020 and coheres with Other Insurance and the 'additional insurance' Extensions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full compliance with all of the terms' is broad but the two-year period is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: CP 01 01 A replaces the Legal Action Against Us condition with a five-year period, so the policy as printed carries two different suit limitations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any revision that would broaden the coverage' is open-textured, but the 45-day window is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c022; nothing else in the instrument addresses mid-term broadening.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single short rule, garbled by OCR but unambiguous in substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c023 and fits the Personal Property Of Others owner-account payment rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pro-rata and excess rules turning on 'the same plan, terms, conditions and provisions', a phrase capable of dispute; the printed text also has stray endorsement wording spliced into it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c024 and interacts with Property Not Covered k. and the excess wording in the trailer extension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As reproduced this 'provision' is an OCR splice of the Calculation of Premium endorsement with the tail of Other Insurance, Policy Period and Transfer of Rights, so it is not a coherent single clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Each of the spliced components is separately reproduced elsewhere (c093, c094), so the instrument contains the same text twice in different arrangements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise temporal and geographic limitation with a closed territory list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates c025; the broader CGL 'coverage territory' definition governs a different coverage part.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite subrogation rule with an enumerated post-loss waiver list; 'must to nothing' is an OCR slip for 'must do nothing'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This printing says 'to or from whom we make payment' while c026 says 'to or for whom', a substantive variance between two printings of the same condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional but definite entitlement to a declared dividend.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Headed as applicable to State Automobile Mutual Insurance Company, whereas the Declarations name State Auto Property and Casualty Insurance Company as the issuing insurer.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise as to membership rights, time and place of meeting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same mismatch: membership rights in the mutual do not obviously follow from a policy issued by the stock property and casualty company named in the Declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence non-assessability warranty; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its promise that no premium other than that stated is payable sits awkwardly with the audit-adjustable premium in the Declarations and the CGL Premium Audit condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line pointer to the definitions section; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section F of CP 10 30 is in fact labelled G. Definitions in this printing, a small cross-reference slip.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Risks Of Direct Physical Loss' is the all-risk trigger and is defined only by subtraction, but that structure is standard and well understood.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Expressly subordinated to Sections B and C of the same form; the Declarations do show Special Form for each item.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The anti-concurrent-causation lead-in ('regardless of any other cause or event that contributes concurrently or in any sequence') is a heavily litigated formulation in general, though its words are emphatic rather than ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs the Ordinance Or Law exclusion that must be reconciled with the Increased Cost of Construction Additional Coverage, which by its terms overrides that exclusion.
